questions.stem: Scenario S1. A prompt says that no refund may be issued before the customer's identity has been verified. The sentence appears once, at the start of a long session, and after many turns the system begins to skip it. What explains this, and where should the requirement live?

options.text: The model loses interest in a rule after a set number of turns, so the sentence is repeated in every user message of the whole session
options.says: Ruled out because the cause is compaction and not boredom, and the remedy is placement: "Put rules that must hold for the whole run in `CLAUDE.md`, or enforce them in a hook."

options.text: The context window resets between turns, so each request must carry the whole conversation by hand
options.says: Ruled out because the window does not reset: "The context window does not reset between turns within a session."

options.text: The sentence is too short to carry weight, so it is lengthened with examples of identity checks
options.says: Ruled out because more words are not the remedy, since a hook "runs on every call, and a prompt does not always"

options.text: Compaction replaces early messages with a summary, so a rule that must hold throughout goes in CLAUDE.md or a hook
options.says: The page says what compaction does (module 45, page 2): "Compaction replaces older messages with a summary, so specific instructions from early in the conversation may not be preserved."

questions.stem: Scenario S1. A customer writes in one message that a refund is wanted on one order, an address has changed, and a charge appears twice. options.text: Pass the whole text to a person

options.text: Work on them in parallel with the shared context they need
options.says: The coordinator lists the items before any tool runs so that each has its own question and its own result, and the guide asks it to "look into each of them in parallel with the shared context they need" (module 48, page 2).

options.text: Run the three matters one after another in a single chain, where each sees the previous conclusion
options.says: Ruled out because each item is worked on with its own question: "Each item is told its own question and not the other items' findings"

options.text: List the matters separately, each with its own question and result
options.says: The coordinator lists the items before any tool runs so that each has its own question and its own result, and the guide asks it to "look into each of them in parallel with the shared context they need" (module 48, page 2).

options.text: Handle only the first matter and ask the customer to send the others separately
options.says: Ruled out because the point of listing first is that "none is lost behind another".

questions.stem: Scenario S1. A refund-limit hook should govern only the coordinator, yet it also fires for subagents that call the same tool. How can it tell the two apart?

options.text: Read the identity fields in its input present only for nested workers

options.text: Use a matcher that names the coordinator in its pattern
options.says: Ruled out because a matcher sees names only: "Matchers only match tool names, not file paths or other arguments."

options.says: Ruled out because a hook set up for the coordinator still fires in its workers: "Hooks fire inside subagents too."

options.text: Wait for a subagent stop event and undo the call afterwards by hand and log it
options.says: Ruled out because a call cannot be undone afterwards: "A post hook can tell the model that something went wrong. It cannot make the refund not have happened."

questions.stem: Scenario S1. A gate refuses a refund because identity is not verified. A teammate suggests that the gate should run the verification itself and carry on. Why not?

options.text: A gate may only read state and can never call a backend service, whatever the rule of the system
options.says: Ruled out because the gate does call the backend after its checks: "For every tool call the model asks for, it checks the prerequisites, and only then does it call the backend."

options.text: Running it would double the cost of every refund request that the desk handles
options.says: Ruled out because the point is honesty and a small gate: "That keeps the conversation honest and keeps the gate small."

options.text: Verification calls are blocked inside any hook or dispatcher by the platform

options.says: The page gives the reason (module 48, page 1): "the customer's identity code is something the model must obtain from the customer, so the gate refuses and says what is missing".

questions.stem: Scenario S1. In a loop built on the SDK, which party should own the decision whether a refund call runs, and where does that decision live?

options.text: The code, in permissions and hooks that act before execution

options.text: The model, through the stop reason of its reply to the call

options.text: The model, by weighing the policy text in its prompt each turn

options.text: Keep three separate tools, because separate names always improve the choice for the model

options.text: Merge them with a tool that infers the verb from the user's message each time

options.text: Treat it as one unit and carry on with the cap check

options.text: Refuse it as malformed, with a result that says what is needed

options.text: In the project's own instruction document, committed so that everyone receives it

options.text: In each engineer's home-folder file, since one exists for every developer

options.text: Checking is weaker, and null passes where a real value belongs
options.says: The page states it (module 62, page 1): "Do not make every field nullable; nullability is for values that can really be absent, since a required field with a valid value is a stronger check."

options.text: Parsing fails whenever one of the fields is left empty or missing
options.says: Ruled out because a field may be missing from the source and then be nullable: "a field that may be missing from the source is optional or nullable"

options.text: The model refuses the whole document whenever one field has no value
options.says: Ruled out because a schema cannot express a refusal, and a missing value is answered with null: "refuse, which a schema cannot express, or fill the field" and "so that `null` is a valid and honest answer"

origin.section: A field that may be absent is nullable

questions.stem: Scenario S6. Two chunks of one document give the vendor as null in the first and as a name with a quote in the second. How does the merge treat that field?

options.text: It keeps the earliest usable entry, with its passage
options.says: The page states the rule (module 62, page 2): "keep the first value that is neither null nor unclear, with the quote it came with".

options.text: It keeps null, the value of the first chunk
options.says: Ruled out because null means the source did not state it: "a field that may be missing from the source is optional or nullable"

options.text: It marks a conflict and asks a person to resolve it by hand
options.says: Ruled out because a conflict needs two real values: "when a later chunk gives a different vendor or total, do not pick silently"

options.text: It joins both into one string separated by a comma and a space
options.says: Ruled out because only line items are joined: "concatenate the line items"

questions.stem: Scenario S6. In a sample of accepted extractions, one wrong item fits no known pattern of mistakes. What does it signal?

options.text: A known weakness, to be logged and then ignored by the team
options.says: Ruled out because new kinds appear when formats change: "the true error rate among accepted items is unknown, and new kinds of error appear when document formats change"

options.text: Noise from random sampling, which more samples will average out later
options.says: Ruled out because the sample does two jobs: "Checking the accepted sample does two jobs."

options.text: A reviewer slip, to be corrected by a second reviewer afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because a single pull says almost nothing about hard strata: "A single random pull from the whole stream is mostly easy cases and says almost nothing about the small, hard strata."

options.text: A new kind of fault, which is the cue to change the pipeline
options.says: The page states it (module 68, page 1): "a wrong item that fits no known pattern is a novel error, which is the signal to change the pipeline".

origin.section: Sample the accepted items by stratum

questions.stem: Scenario S6. On a labelled set, a team wants the precision of automation at a candidate confidence cut-off of 85. How is it measured?

options.text: Average the confidence values of the items that fall below 85 on the set
options.says: Ruled out because the first step groups by confidence: "Group the labelled items by the confidence they were given."

options.text: Take the items just under 85 and count how many of them are wrong
options.says: Ruled out because items below the cut-off are not what automation accepts: "Everything below it goes to a person."

options.text: Take every item at or above 85 and see what share of them is right
options.says: The page states it (module 68, page 1): "For a candidate threshold, take every item at or above it, and measure how many are right. This is the precision of automation at that threshold."

options.text: Sample the accepted items by stratum and take the mean of the sample
options.says: Ruled out because stratified sampling is a different job: "The sample must be random within each stratum"
